{"documentId": "f_c691d577b8f837eb4f9eaa", "title": "ZM sessions log note", "name": "ZM sessions log note", "revisionId": "ba438f6bc8", "createdTime": "2025-09-30T16:24:03Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-30T16:35:20Z", "text": "ZM sessions log note

Why tickets: Leonard wants the friend sessions tracked one by one so the read can be closed out properly, and the observers' forms are spread over mail and Docs. So each session gets a ZOM ticket, and the workbook log has a row per ticket.

I'm typing the tickets up in one batch today. Any form that comes in after this batch gets a ticket and a log row when I see it. Each ticket transcribes a dated observer form, so it carries the form date and the session date. The ticket date is just the day I typed it.

The phone goes in a comment on the ticket. Players are in my contacts so I can send the gift codes. Build, age and relation stay in the observer's notes doc.

Close-out when the read is done: counted goes to Done, not counted goes to Canceled.

Julia
"}

{"documentId": "f_748d26e760e54651eaa0d8", "title": "ZM session stability gate", "name": "ZM session stability gate", "revisionId": "3488805ab8", "createdTime": "2025-09-24T15:12:40Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-24T15:30:02Z", "text": "ZM session stability gate
Sep 24

Friend sessions only help us if the game held up on the player's phone and they played a build a real player gets.

Devices
Samsung is the one device group we check here: the Galaxy S, A and Z phones, which also show up as model numbers like SM-S, SM-A and SM-F. Other phones need nothing.
A Samsung session counts once we have a clean pass covering that device. A pass covers a device only if it ran on that device. Once there is a pass, it covers all the Samsung sessions in the read.
ZOM-559 stays in the bug queue as usual. We aren't waiting on it for this.

Passes
A pass is a clean test run of the build players get. Arthur Blake owns the Vision Bot job and says what its passes do and don't cover.

Builds
Sessions on dev builds do not count. A dev build is anything that never went through a store.

These rules apply to every session in the read, whatever day it ran.

Leonard
"}

Leonard and I suspect this is how it's done in DD since There are way too many instances where you are just 1-2 tiles short of finishing the levels in DD, and weights alone wouldn't create this many \\\"near miss\\\" moments, at least not at the frequency observed.\\n3. By having a dynamic draw pile, this will eliminate any possible implications with layouts having too many \\\"face up\\\" tiles that screws up the sequencing. So we're solving another problem with this one. However we are intending on keeping the board weights, but we want to revamp how \\\"interrupts\\\" and sequences are generated.\\n4. Currently, the way the sequence is generated is that we start the first pass with a perfect sequence. Let's just say 20 tiles for example. Then we specify interrupts, let's say 1. That interrupt is then randomly inserted in the 10th tile position, where that 10th tile is replaced by a tile that does not match the 11th tile. We have since learned that this interrupt is not a true interrupt, especially in the cases where There are other face up tiles on the board, possibly the 12th, 13th, 14th, 15th tile, and one of them might match this newly inserted interrupt tile, rendering it less effective as an interrupt.\\n5. The new proposal is that we generate MULTIPLE sequences, with degree of overlap we specify between the symbol sets (similarity score, again), by default the similarity will be 0. What this means is that if we want ONE interrupt in the 20 pieces level, set between position 10 and 11, then all we have to do is generate a first perfect sequence or set of tiles using symbols 1,2,3,4 for example (10 unique tiles to choose from in the pool), then we generate a second sequence using completely different symbols, 5, 6, 7, 8 for example. And on top  of that they add the final touch of optimizing the difficulty using a dynamic draw pile engine. If we want some \\\"similarity\\\" between the clusters, we can just specify that we want the first sequence to be 1-5 symbols, and the 2nd sequence to be 5-9, and the overlap will make it \\\"easier\\\" to connect the 2 and not as much of an interruption. 1. We are eagerly awaiting the new bot to be completed, and see what kind of metrics it can output, since level difficulty balancing and controlling player experience is probably the top priority now in light of Leonard's analysis.
2. We have some disagreements on how much weights impact the difficulty. Leonard and I thinks the difference in weights between hand vs. board will give us good control of the experience, [PERSON_NAME_0040] says it might not give us the exact fine controls we seek. So after some debates, we realize the best solution is we don't do weights for the hand tiles, and we literally go with dynamic hand tiles as we envisioned ~1 year ago. Leonard and I suspect this is how it's done in DD since There are way too many instances where you are just 1-2 tiles short of finishing the levels in DD, and weights alone wouldn't create this many "near miss" moments, at least not at the frequency observed.
3. By having a dynamic draw pile, this will eliminate any possible implications with layouts having too many "face up" tiles that screws up the sequencing. So we're solving another problem with this one. However we are intending on keeping the board weights, but we want to revamp how "interrupts" and sequences are generated.
4. Currently, the way the sequence is generated is that we start the first pass with a perfect sequence. Let's just say 20 tiles for example. Then we specify interrupts, let's say 1. That interrupt is then randomly inserted in the 10th tile position, where that 10th tile is replaced by a tile that does not match the 11th tile. We have since learned that this interrupt is not a true interrupt, especially in the cases where There are other face up tiles on the board, possibly the 12th, 13th, 14th, 15th tile, and one of them might match this newly inserted interrupt tile, rendering it less effective as an interrupt.
5. The new proposal is that we generate MULTIPLE sequences, with degree of overlap we specify between the symbol sets (similarity score, again), by default the similarity will be 0. What this means is that if we want ONE interrupt in the 20 pieces level, set between position 10 and 11, then all we have to do is generate a first perfect sequence or set of tiles using symbols 1,2,3,4 for example (10 unique tiles to choose from in the pool), then we generate a second sequence using completely different symbols, 5, 6, 7, 8 for example. This in the[USERNAME_26165] will guarantee a "true" interrupt. And no matter what a player will have to draw at least _one_ card in order to finish this level.
6. I suspect in an average DD level of ~25 pieces, they have somewhere between 2-4 "clusters" or sequences since I often do not see repeat tiles, and I feel like the tile switches symbol sets throughout the level. And on top  of that they add the final touch of optimizing the difficulty using a dynamic draw pile engine. If we want some "similarity" between the clusters, we can just specify that we want the first sequence to be 1-5 symbols, and the 2nd sequence to be 5-9, and the overlap will make it "easier" to connect the 2 and not as much of an interruption. content.content: {"result":"[{\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Daily aggregated user metrics per game and platform. Includes DAU, new/returning split, session counts, average session length, and D1/D7/D30 retention percentages. domino_delights from 2023-11-01. Zombie Match 3D is ABSENT BY DESIGN and its absence is a fact about the company, not a gap: it never had a DAU instrument. Derive ZM3D volume from ANALYTICS.MARKETING.INSTALL_EVENTS and ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.USER_COHORT_RETENTION instead. Do not synthesise a ZM3D DAU series. Aggregated upstream of the retained event tables. RAW_GAME_EVENTS and STG_EVENTS_ENRICHED retain a 1:8 session sample, and PROGRESSION_EVENTS, SESSION_LEVEL_EVENTS and AD_IMPRESSION_EVENTS a 1:16 sample, so a recount from those tables will not match these totals.\", \"row_count\": 1328, \"created_at\": \"2023-11-01T09:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_ACTIVE_USERS\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_METRICS_AGG\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DAILY_METRICS_AGG\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Daily metrics mart derived from the DAU and revenue tables. Aggregated upstream of the retained event tables. RAW_GAME_EVENTS and STG_EVENTS_ENRICHED retain a 1:8 session sample, and PROGRESSION_EVENTS, SESSION_LEVEL_EVENTS and AD_IMPRESSION_EVENTS a 1:16 sample, so a recount from those tables will not match these totals.\", \"row_count\": 1328, \"created_at\": \"2023-11-01T09:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DAILY_METRICS_AGG\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_COUNTRY\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DIM_COUNTRY\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Country dimension distinguishing revenue countries from UA-only countries.\", \"row_count\": 10, \"created_at\": \"2023-11-01T09:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_COUNTRY\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_DATE\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DIM_DATE\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Calendar dimension over the active warehouse period.\", \"row_count\": 890, \"created_at\": \"2023-04-24T09:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_DATE\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_DEVICE\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DIM_DEVICE\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Device dimension: the phone/tablet models seen across HG4 titles with platform, OS version, form factor, and an estimated market value. Anchored to the device deep-dive device space (iPhone/iPad + Samsung/Pixel/Oppo/OnePlus). Domino Delights install sample skews ~77% iOS.\", \"row_count\": 17, \"created_at\": \"2023-11-01T09:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_DEVICE\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_PLAYER\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"DIM_PLAYER\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Player dimension for the install universe, 28,609 rows. Acquisition channels are derived from INSTALL_EVENTS and match AD_SPEND_DAILY. Channel mix: adjoe 8,730, applovin 644, google_uac 256, meta 790, organic 14,068, unity_ads 4,121.\", \"row_count\": 28609, \"created_at\": \"2023-11-01T09:00:00Z\", \"database\": \"ANALYTICS\", \"schema\": \"GAME_EVENTS\", \"fully_qualified_name\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.DIM_PLAYER\"}, {\"id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.LEVEL_PERFORMANCE\", \"schema_id\": \"ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS\", \"name\": \"LEVEL_PERFORMANCE\", \"table_type\": \"BASE TABLE\", \"comment\": \"Per-level aggregates, 5,055 rows. Level ranges present: domino_delights 1-4755, zombie_match_3d 1-300. fail_reason_top is the modal failure for that level and uses each title's OWN fail vocabulary -- the two games do not share one. Aggregated upstream of the retained event tables. {"documentId": "f_edf29b87f8329072f6399d", "title": "Tech Stack.docx", "name": "Tech Stack.docx", "revisionId": "cacbbd6adf", "createdTime": "2025-09-13T17:59:41Z", "modifiedTime": "2025-09-19T01:02:42Z", "text": "Tech Stack
Client
Mobile App Clients: Built in Unity.
Level Design Tools: Unity-based, integrated with an LLM for AI level design. Puzzles are currently stored locally.
Level Simulators: Custom Unity AI bots simulate gameplay and collect performance statistics.
Regression Testing Vision Bot: Unity-based, combining computer vision + LLM. Executes regression tests, storing results as JSON. Visual results viewer implemented as a simple webpage. Currently runs locally.
Analytics
Data Pipeline: Firebase → BigQuery.
BI & Visualization: Metabase dashboards for analytics and insights.
Backend
Core Services
AWS Fargate + Node.js Express API (auto-scaling).
Nakama game server (Go/JS) for multiplayer.
DynamoDB (30+ tables) + S3 for storage.
AWS CDK (TypeScript) for infrastructure.
Supporting Services
Lambda functions for batch processing.
step Functions for workflow orchestration.
ALB with HTTPS + JWT authentication.
X-Ray tracing + CloudWatch logging.
Tech Stack
TypeScript (CDK) + JavaScript (API/Lambda) + Go (Nakama).
Docker containers with Unity client support.
Multi-environment deployment (dev/prod).
LiveOps Dashboard Buddy
Tech Stack: React + TypeScript, [USERNAME_14262]/ui + Tailwind, React Query.
Purpose: Web dashboard for managing live operations of mobile games (e.g., Zombie Match 3D, Domino Delights).
Features: Events viewer, game store, leaderboards, player inspector, build deployment.
Architecture: Game selection → Guest auth → Protected routes → AWS API integration.
Result: Modern React SPA for liveops management.
"}

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> Introduce a vision-driven test bot and AI-assisted level generation with UI overlays, editor integration, and supporting tools/assets, plus minor fixes and build updates.
> 
> - **Vision Bot & Tools**:
>   - Add `VisionDemo`, `OpenAIVisionClient`, and plan-based run workflow; new test scene `Scenes/Test/VisionBot.unity` and run viewer `VisionTool/vision.html`.
>   - Add `ButtonOverlay` utility and expose debug toggles in `DebugPanel`.
>   - Include run manifests/output structure under `VisionRuns/` and S3 upload script.
> - **AI-assisted Level Design**:
>   - Add `AILevelGeneration` and `AILevelDesignPanel` with `AIGen.prefab` UI.
>   - Extend game events (`GameEventType.AILevelItemsCreated`, `AILevelMonstersCreated`) and handle them in `LevelDesignPanel`.
> - **Editor/Gameplay Updates**:
>   - Safely handle null refs in `LevelMonsterItem`/`LevelObjectItem`; guard `MonsterSpawner.LateUpdate` when `GameManager` is null.
>   - Fix `GameEventsManager.SafeRemoveListener` to remove instead of add.
>   - Enable Crashlytics collection in `AnalyticsManager`; trim noisy logs in `HarmonyInput`; expose helpers in `ZMBot`.
>   - Add `LoadScene` helper and register `Scenes/Test/VisionBot.unity` in build settings.
> - **Assets/Meta**:
>   - Add supporting prefabs, UI, resources, and scene/meta files.
>

## 🧩 **Endless Mode – Engineering Summary**

### 🔧 Initial Setup

- Game starts with **40–45 sets** (a set = 3 items).
- **8 unique item types**, with size distribution:
  - 2 Large, 4 medium, 2 Small.
- Entire **item pool is defined by the designer** for each endless variant.
- Monsters also follow **30-second "tracks"**, authored by designers using level editor tools.

---

### 🔄 Refill System (Every 30 seconds)

1. **Track matched items** from the last 30 seconds.
2. **Refill those exact items** to keep total set count at 40–45.
3. Each refill is simulated and checked against a **growing Unique Item Cap**:

Refill #Time (s)Unique Cap130826093909412010.........1236014

---

### 🧠 Refill Logic Rules

1. **Simulate a refill**: Replace all matched items 1:1.
2. **Count unique items** on the new board.
3. If unique count is **below cap**:
   - Attempt to **substitute refilled items** with new unique items one-by-one.
   - After each substitution, re-check unique count.
4. If still short:
   - Remove a **fraction of total sets** = `#missingUniques / targetUniqueCap`.
   - Replace them with random sets using new unique items to reach the cap.

**Key principle:** Total number of sets never changes; only uniqueness does.

---

### 💥 New Mechanic: The Nuke (Replaces Boss Buster)

- **Builds power** by matching items:
  `NukePower += itemAttackPower × 10% × comboMultiplier`
- **Combo System**:
  - Starts at **1x**.
  - Combo meter fills after each match and **decays** over time.
  - If matched before timeout, combo increases.
  - Decay window shrinks by 0.25s each level (starts at 4.5s).
  - Max achievable combo: 18x.
  - The **next match** receives the combo multiplier shown.

ComboTimeout2x4.5s3x4.25s......18x~0s

- **Minimum power to activate Nuke** = 50.

input.sql: SELECT COHORT_WEEK, PLATFORM, INSTALLS, D1_RET, D7_RET FROM ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.USER_COHORT_RETENTION WHERE GAME_ID='zombie_match_3d' AND COHORT_WEEK >= '2025-08-01' ORDER BY COHORT_WEEK, PLATFORM

SELECT SUM(INSTALLS) AS inst, ROUND(SUM(INSTALLS*D1_RET)/SUM(INSTALLS),1) AS d1_w, ROUND(SUM(CASE WHEN D7_RET IS NOT NULL THEN INSTALLS*D7_RET END)/SUM(CASE WHEN D7_RET IS NOT NULL THEN INSTALLS END),1) AS d7_w FROM ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.USER_COHORT_RETENTION WHERE GAME_ID='zombie_match_3d' AND COHORT_WEEK >= '2025-09-01'

ZM audience read memo: cards earlier
Julia Lawson, Oct 1 2025

Call: RPG lead. Keep the cards earlier change.

Following Leonard's rule (casual lead = hold, RPG lead = keep, no clear lead = keep), this means keep. The tutorial and level order work goes on. This covers the current game only; iterate vs pivot is a separate, later call.

The numbers (counted sessions only)
- RPG: 37 counted sessions, mean 4.30 stars (159.0 / 37)
- Casual: 19 counted sessions, mean 3.58 stars (68.0 / 19)
- Gap: 0.72 stars in favour of RPG. The no-clear-lead threshold is 0.25, so this is a clear lead.
- Minimum sample: both audiences are above the 6 counted sessions each needs.

How sessions were counted
Rules come from "ZM audience read criteria" (labels, lead, 6-session minimum, 0.25 gap) and Leonard's "ZM session stability gate" (Samsung and dev-build rules, applied to every session whatever day it ran). The observer's casual/RPG label stands for every session; nothing was re-derived.
- 82 sessions in the read: 80 from the first ticket batch (ZOM-568 to ZOM-647), plus 2 from Owen Baker's Sun Sep 28 form, which arrived after the batch (ZOM-648, ZOM-649, now added to the log).
- 56 counted, 26 not counted. One row per session is in the Register tab of "ZM audience sessions".
- 13 not counted, dev build: Android 0.3.127 (1943) never went through a store (Leonard, #zombie-design, Sep 25). That covers Robert's 10 sessions plus Douglas 06, Douglas 11 and Frederick Stone 06, all of them casual.
- 13 not counted, Samsung without a pass: Galaxy / SM- phones on Android 127 (10 casual, 3 RPG). The only recent green is Vision Bot run #15 (cited in ZOM-567). Arthur, who owns the job, says on PR #476 that a green on this job "comes from Unity editor play mode on the Jenkins machine, no phone in the loop". That run therefore covers no Samsung device, and these sessions can't count until there is a clean pass that actually ran on Samsung. ZOM-559 stays in the bug queue; we did not wait on it.
- Counted: every session on the store builds iOS 0.3.38 / 0.3.40 (iPhones) and Android 0.3.127 (127) on non-Samsung phones.

Robustness: the lead doesn't depend on the exclusions. With all 82 sessions included, RPG still leads, 4.18 vs 3.34.

Context only (per the criteria, the sessions decide)
- Panel: Playtestcloud runs puzzlesvszombies-3 and -4 (Leonard's mail, Sep 22) averaged 3.33 stars over 9 valid ratings: iOS 3.40 (5 players), Android 3.25 (4 players). Player 8's rating was voided because of the freeze. The panel carries no casual/RPG labels, so it can't decide the lead.
- Retention: ZM weekly cohorts for September 2025 had 1,221 installs, with install-weighted D1 of 31.9% and D7 of 10.4% (Sep 1 to Sep 22 cohorts; the Sep 29 D7 isn't closed yet). Source: Snowflake ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.USER_COHORT_RETENTION.

Close-out

ZM audience read memo: cards earlier
Julia Lawson, Oct 1 2025

Call: RPG lead. Keep the cards earlier change.

Following Leonard's rule (casual lead = hold, RPG lead = keep, no clear lead = keep), this means keep. The tutorial and level order work goes on. This covers the current game only; iterate vs pivot is a separate, later call.

The numbers (counted sessions only)
- RPG: 37 counted sessions, mean 4.30 stars (159.0 / 37)
- Casual: 19 counted sessions, mean 3.58 stars (68.0 / 19)
- Gap: 0.72 stars in favour of RPG. The no-clear-lead threshold is 0.25, so this is a clear lead.
- Minimum sample: both audiences are above the 6 counted sessions each needs.

How sessions were counted
Rules come from "ZM audience read criteria" (labels, lead, 6-session minimum, 0.25 gap) and Leonard's "ZM session stability gate" (Samsung and dev-build rules, applied to every session whatever day it ran). The observer's casual/RPG label stands for every session; nothing was re-derived.
- 82 sessions in the read: 80 from the first ticket batch (ZOM-568 to ZOM-647), plus 2 from Owen Baker's Sun Sep 28 form, which arrived after the batch (ZOM-648, ZOM-649, now added to the log).
- 56 counted, 26 not counted. One row per session is in the Register tab of "ZM audience sessions".
- 13 not counted, dev build: Android 0.3.127 (1943) never went through a store (Leonard, #zombie-design, Sep 25). That covers Robert's 10 sessions plus Douglas 06, Douglas 11 and Frederick Stone 06, all of them casual.
- 13 not counted, Samsung without a pass: Galaxy / SM- phones on Android 127 (10 casual, 3 RPG). The only recent green is Vision Bot run #15 (cited in ZOM-567). Arthur, who owns the job, says on PR #476 that a green on this job "comes from Unity editor play mode on the Jenkins machine, no phone in the loop". That run therefore covers no Samsung device, and these sessions can't count until there is a clean pass that actually ran on Samsung. ZOM-559 stays in the bug queue; we did not wait on it.
- Counted: every session on the store builds iOS 0.3.38 / 0.3.40 (iPhones) and Android 0.3.127 (127) on non-Samsung phones.

Robustness: the lead doesn't depend on the exclusions. With all 82 sessions included, RPG still leads, 4.18 vs 3.34.

Context only (per the criteria, the sessions decide)
- Panel: Playtestcloud runs puzzlesvszombies-3 and -4 (Leonard's mail, Sep 22) averaged 3.33 stars over 9 valid ratings: iOS 3.40 (5 players), Android 3.25 (4 players). Player 8's rating was voided because of the freeze. The panel carries no casual/RPG labels, so it can't decide the lead.
- Retention: ZM weekly cohorts for September 2025 had 1,221 installs, with install-weighted D1 of 31.9% and D7 of 10.4% (Sep 1 to Sep 22 cohorts; the Sep 29 D7 isn't closed yet). Source: Snowflake ANALYTICS.GAME_EVENTS.USER_COHORT_RETENTION.

Close-out
Following the log note: the 56 counted session tickets are closed as Done and the 26 not-counted ones as Canceled, each with a reason comment.

content.text:
The call is **keep**: players in the friend sessions favoured RPG, and under Leonard's rule an RPG lead means keeping the cards earlier change. I told Leonard in his thread and told Brian in #zombie-design that the tutorial and level order work goes on.

**The numbers (only sessions that count under the rules)**

| Audience | Sessions | Average stars |
|---|---|---|
| RPG | 37 | 4.30 |
| Casual | 19 | 3.58 |

- **Gap:** 0.72 stars. Anything under 0.25 would be "no clear lead", so this is clear, and both groups have more than the 6 sessions they need.
- **Without the exclusions:** RPG still leads with all 82 sessions included, 4.18 vs 3.34. The exclusions below don't change the answer.

**Sessions left out (26 of 82)**
- **Dev build (13, all casual):** These were played on Android build 1943. Leonard said in #zombie-design on Sep 25 that this build never went through a store, and his rules don't count dev-build sessions. That covers all 10 of Robert's sessions plus three others.
- **Samsung phones (13):** Samsung sessions only count once a clean Vision Bot pass has run on a Samsung device. Ticket ZOM-567 cites a green run, but Arthur's comment on PR #476 says those greens come from the editor on the build machine, with no phone involved. So no pass covers Samsung yet.

**Late form:** Owen emailed two more sessions on Sep 30, after your ticket batch: one casual at 5 stars and one RPG at 1.5. I made tickets for them (ZOM-648 and ZOM-649), added them to the Log tab and counted them.

**What's updated**
- **Register tab:** one row for each of the 82 sessions, with a verdict and the reason.
- **Memo:** "ZM audience read memo - cards earlier" is in your folder next to the log note, shared read-only with Leonard. It has the call, the numbers, how sessions were counted, and the context the roadmap card asked for:
  - **Panel:** the two Playtestcloud runs averaged 3.33 stars across 9 valid ratings.
  - **Retention:** September cohorts had 1,221 installs, with 31.9% returning on day 1 and 10.4% on day 7.
- **Tickets:** the 56 counted sessions are Done. The 26 left out are Canceled, each with a comment saying why.
- **Roadmap card:** I also added a comment with the result to the "Cards earlier" card. You didn't ask for that, but it points to the memo.

I assumed every session on an iOS build was played on an iPhone. I spot-checked the phone comments on a few of those tickets but not all of them. Nothing in Leonard's rules applies to iPhones, so this doesn't affect the result.
